post.description:
Create a new task.

Runtime + identity resolution is JWT-claim-driven (see
`docs/design/sdk-api.md`). When the caller authenticates with a
CP-minted **runner JWT** (`token_type == "runner"`), the claims
carry the resolved `runtime_id`, optional `experiment_id`, and
`identity` — DP looks up the recipe pin via the resolver and
stamps everything onto the task, ignoring any body `runtime_id`.
A non-runner credential (session/browser, internal service tokens)
carries no runtime claim; it may bind a runtime by passing
`runtime_id` in the body (validated against the caller's project),
otherwise the task runs against the project's default agent path.
The same split applies to `bindings_required`: a runner's claim is
authoritative, and a non-runner caller sets it in the body.

Provisions a sandbox. The sandbox reads INTROSPECTION_AGENT_NAME from its
environment to select the managed Pi agent definition.

Requires scope: `tasks:write`, `write`, or `*`

get.description:
Get a task by ID.

By default this is the cheapest read available: a single-row lookup of the
task projection from Postgres, with **no** enrichment and **no** Restate
round-trip. The ``status`` field is maintained on the row by the task
workflow, so this is the quick way to check a task's status (e.g. a readiness
poll or catch-up read) without loading Restate.

Anything that costs more than that bare read is opt-in via ``?include=`` (a
repeatable query param, see ``TaskInclude``). ``?include=agent`` enriches an
interactive, in-flight task with live sandbox status from the Restate
workflow — one extra round-trip — so the interactive task-detail view opts in
while status checks do not. Live, ongoing output belongs on ``/stream`` (SSE);
this endpoint never streams.

Requires scope: `tasks:read`, `read`, or `*`

parameters.name: include

schema.description: Opt-in non-default enrichments (e.g. `agent` for live sandbox status); repeatable
schema.title: Include

parameters.description: Opt-in non-default enrichments (e.g. `agent` for live sandbox status); repeatable

delete.description:
Cancel any active work and soft-delete a task in one operation.

Requires scope: ``tasks:delete``, ``delete``, or ``*``

post.description:
Create a run on an interactive task.

Running tasks receive steering guidance. Idle/pending tasks receive a prompt.
Completed, failed, or unavailable sandboxes are restarted implicitly.
This is the existing interactive-task subresource surface; new resources
should still use CRUD-shaped routes.

Cancel the current run for an active interactive task.

Default (including the bodyless call) **aborts**: the in-flight turn is
interrupted immediately and the sandbox stays warm, so the task returns to
``idle`` and the same container is resumable on the next prompt. Pass
``mode=drain`` to instead let the active turn finish and tear the sandbox
down at the next settle boundary so the next prompt cold-boots on the
current base image — the release/rollover path
(docs/design/sandbox-drain-on-release.md).

get.description: Get status for a task run on the existing interactive-task subresource.

Stream AG-UI output for one task run.

``wait_for_start`` **defaults to ``true``** — the legacy long-poll: the
server holds the stream open, emitting ``queued``/``starting`` lifecycle
frames, until the run is live. This default exists for backward
compatibility with clients that do not send the param (notably the SDKs,
which call the bare endpoint). Pass ``wait_for_start=0`` to opt into the
target "not ready, retry" contract: a pre-hardware run first holds up to
the advertised ``Retry-After`` window; only if it remains not attachable
does it return ``429`` + ``Retry-After`` + a ``{"status": <phase>}`` body.
Our own clients (frontend, capacity harness) send ``0``; the default flips
to ``0`` (or the param is removed) once every client — including the
external SDKs — has migrated.

The reconnect resume cursor — the last content-frame seq the client
received (the SSE ``id:`` of worker content frames) — arrives either as
``since`` (explicit query form, our frontend) or as the SSE-standard
``Last-Event-ID`` header (the SDKs' ``streamResumable``, see
``docs/design/sdk-resumable-streams.md``). It is forwarded to the
runtime-worker so it replays the frames the client missed while
disconnected, or opens with a ``MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT`` when the disconnect
outlived its bounded replay buffer; a runtime ``410`` passes through.
Non-numeric header values
(connection-local ``c-…`` control-frame ids) are not cursors and are
ignored.

post.description:
Archive a task, cancelling any active work in the background.

Always sets ``is_archived = true``. If the task is still active,
also cancels the Restate workflow so the sandbox is cleaned up.

Requires scope: ``tasks:write``, ``write``, or ``*``
Unarchive a task so it can accept new runs.

patch.description:
Update an automation. `kind` and `trigger_type` are immutable, and so is
the group of a Restate-backed automation.

The read and the write take separate sessions so no connection is held
across the control-plane reads between them; `expected_updated_at` makes
the write apply only to the revision that was checked.

post.description:
Run an automation now.

Retained from the control-plane router it replaces, and synchronous for the
reason it can now afford to be: the task it creates is local.

⚠️ Every read opens its own short-lived session and closes it. An injected
`DbReadSession` would pin its pooled connection for the WHOLE request —
autocommit releases the transaction, not the checkout — and this handler
goes on to call the control plane, ClickHouse, Restate and a sandbox
launch. Slow or concurrent manual triggers would exhaust the pool with no
database work in flight.
Record a command and send it to the task's workflow; poll the row (or wait on the read) for the outcome.

post.description:
Create a file.

Multipart requests upload a new binary file. JSON requests create or
version text content by name. File content is limited to 50 MB.

Both shapes accept optional `tags` (repeated `tags` form fields, or a JSON
array), stamped on the file when the request creates it, as on a task.
Both also accept an optional `ttl_seconds`, which stamps `expires_at` on
the row so a maintenance sweep soft-deletes it and reclaims its storage
object once that instant passes. Omit it and the file never expires.

Requires scope: `files:write`, `write`, or `*`

Requires scope: `files:read`, `read`, or `*`

get.description:
List GenAI conversations with filtering and pagination.

Requires scope: `conversations:read`, `read`, or `*`

Returns aggregated conversation summaries from ClickHouse traces.
A conversation may contain multiple traces linked by conversation ID, and
the summary aggregates metrics across those traces.

**Ownership:**
Non-privileged callers see only their own conversations (owner-key scoped,
same predicate as item/detail reads). Valid `share_id` capabilities widen
the page with the conversations those shares grant.

**Pagination:**
Use the `next` token from the response to fetch subsequent pages.
The token encodes the cursor position and must be passed unchanged.

**Filtering:**
All filters are optional and combined with AND logic.
Date range filters are inclusive.

SidecarBuild.title: SidecarBuild
SidecarBuild.description:
Compose ``build``: the context the plane builds this service from.

``context`` is a Files API object id (a ``.tar.gz`` of the build context),
never a host path or a git URL: the plane has no filesystem the caller can
name, and a build's input has always been an object the caller could
already write. Compose's short form ``build: <context>`` is accepted and
means the same thing.

Every other compose ``build`` key (``args``, ``target``, ``secrets``,
``ssh``, ``cache_from``, ``network``, ``no_cache``, ``pull``, ``labels``
…) is refused by name through ``extra="forbid"``, like the rest of the
compose surface.

TaskCancelMode.title: TaskCancelMode
TaskCancelMode.description:
How a task run cancel behaves.

``abort`` interrupts the in-flight turn immediately and keeps the sandbox
warm, so the task drops back to ``idle`` and the same container is resumable
on the next prompt — what an interactive "stop" button wants. ``drain`` lets
the active turn finish and return control to the user, then tears the sandbox
down at the next settle boundary (the task lands terminal/``cancelled`` and
the next prompt cold-boots on the current base image) — the release path.
See docs/design/sandbox-drain-on-release.md.

mode.description: Cancel behaviour: 'abort' (default) interrupts the in-flight turn now and keeps the sandbox warm/resumable; 'drain' lets the turn finish then tears the sandbox down at the next settle boundary (task -> cancelled). The bodyless call aborts.

drain_within_seconds.title: Drain Within Seconds
drain_within_seconds.description: Drain only: force teardown if the task has not reached a settle boundary within this many seconds. Omit to wait, bounded by the deployment drain ceiling.

TaskCancelRequest.title: TaskCancelRequest
TaskCancelRequest.description:
Options for cancelling a task run.

Default (and the bodyless call) **aborts**: the in-flight turn is interrupted
immediately and the sandbox stays warm, so the task returns to ``idle`` and
the same container is resumable. Pass ``mode=drain`` to instead let the active
turn finish and tear the sandbox down at the next settle boundary (the task
lands ``cancelled`` and the next prompt cold-boots on the current base image);
a drained ``awaiting_user`` task keeps its ``metadata.pending_interrupts`` so
the HITL resume path rehydrates the question on the fresh sandbox.
See docs/design/sandbox-drain-on-release.md.

TaskCancelResponse.title: TaskCancelResponse
TaskCancelResponse.description: Response returned after cancelling a task run.

TaskCompose.title: TaskCompose
TaskCompose.description:
The compose document that makes up a task's world: its services and named volumes.

Accepts the compose file's own ``services`` mapping with ``main`` in it
(Harbor's shape) and lifts ``main`` into its own field, so the persisted
form is explicit about which entry is the agent slot.

kind.description: Execution shape. `agent` (default) is a conversation; `eval` is the same shape run as an evaluation trial, governed separately at admission. `process` is internal-only and rejected here.

agent_name.title: Agent Name
agent_name.description: Recipe agent to run; omitted -> the recipe default (agents/agent.yaml)

runtime_id.title: Runtime Id
runtime_id.description: Runtime to bind this task to. Ignored when the caller presents a runner credential (the JWT claim is authoritative); honored for non-runner session/browser callers and validated against the caller's project.

bindings_required.title: Bindings Required
bindings_required.description: Whether the runtime's application-identity MCP bindings (`kind=mcp` endpoints gated on `endpoints.authorized_application_id`) must materialize. `false` drops them from the session bootstrap and names them in `unavailable_mcp_bindings`, so the agent starts without those tools; it only ever removes credentials. Ignored for a runner credential (the JWT claim is authoritative). Omitted -> required.

recipe_git_commit_sha.title: Recipe Git Commit Sha
recipe_git_commit_sha.description: Exact pushed Recipe commit to materialize for an evaluation task. The bound Runtime remains authoritative for the repository, image, subpath, and Runtime identity. Requires `kind: eval`.

recipe_patch.description: Operator-only development input. The patch File must belong to the authenticated Operator Task and match the selected Runtime's deployed Recipe checkout. Other callers are rejected.

repositories.title: Repositories
repositories.description: Workspace repositories to clone into the sandbox's workspace/repos/ for this task: {repo, ref?, depth?}. Each repo must be listed in the runtime's runtime.github.repositories grant (and registered to the caller's project) — the recipe decides what may be cloned, this list decides what is cloned and at what ref. Omit `ref` for the repository's default branch — the clone takes the remote's HEAD, so nothing is stored or kept in sync — and `depth` defaults to a shallow clone. An entry outside the grant, or one that fails to resolve at launch, is logged and dropped, never a launch failure.

idle_timeout_seconds.title: Idle Timeout Seconds
idle_timeout_seconds.description: Override the interactive idle window (seconds) before the sandbox is torn down. 0 tears down as soon as it's provisioned (e.g. an empty-prompt warm/bake run); omit to use the deployment default. Clamped to the task timeout.

conversation_metadata.title: Conversation Metadata
conversation_metadata.description: Immutable filter dimensions for the conversation this task creates. Filter the resulting conversation with GET /v1/conversations?metadata=key:value. Keys must be one level ([A-Za-z0-9_-], no `.`), values must be non-empty strings of at most 1024 characters, and at most 64 keys are accepted. These dimensions land in append-only telemetry and cannot later be edited or deleted.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Free-form tags to stamp on the task at create time, conventionally 'key:value' (e.g. 'team:acme'). Filter with `?tag=team:acme`. Shared: any member whose own tags intersect these can read and write the task, so tagging is how a task is handed to a cohort.

files.title: Files
files.description: Files API references to attach to this task. Materialized into the sandbox workspace at boot and announced to the agent. Equivalent to setting metadata.conversation_files.uploads, which stays accepted.

commands.title: Commands
commands.description: Accept commands on POST /v1/tasks/{id}/commands (exec, upload, download) for this evaluation trial. Off by default: a trial that only needs its agent to run never opens the exec surface. Requires `kind: eval`.

compose.description: Compose services to run beside the agent for an evaluation trial, in the task's own `docker-compose.yaml` shape: a `services` mapping (`main` is the agent slot and may carry only `volumes` and `depends_on`) plus named `volumes`. Each other service becomes a container of the sandbox pod, fresh per task, reachable from the agent by its service name on the pod's loopback, under the same gVisor sandbox and NetworkPolicy as the agent, as a distinct non-root user with none of the runtime's platform environment. Supported per service: image, command, entrypoint, environment, working_dir, expose/ports (container port only), healthcheck, named volumes, depends_on, deploy.resources. Anything a pod cannot honour (network_mode, networks, extra_hosts, privileged, cap_add, devices, bind mounts, build, user) is refused by name. Only `kind: eval` tasks may carry it, and such a task always runs in-cluster.

fork_share_id.title: Fork Share Id
fork_share_id.description: Fork from a shared conversation: the /v1/shares grant id for the source conversation. Persisted into metadata.forked_response and used by the runtime as the read capability when hydrating the forked history — it is itself the permissions boundary, so no share lookup happens at create. The fork seeds the new task with the whole shared conversation.

TaskCreate.title: TaskCreate
TaskCreate.description:
Schema for creating a task.

Runner credentials remain authoritative for runtime selection: a runner JWT
(or the in-process MCP override) always wins. Non-runner (session/browser)
callers, which carry no runtime claim, may bind a runtime by passing
``runtime_id`` in the body — it is validated against the caller's project at
create time.

TaskCreateResponse.title: TaskCreateResponse
TaskCreateResponse.description: Response returned after creating a task and its initial run.

id.title: Id
id.description: Files API file id

name.title: Name
name.description: Workspace-relative name to mount the file as. Optional — the Files API already knows the file's name, so supply this only to override it (mount under a different name, or nest it in a subdirectory).

size_bytes.title: Size Bytes
size_bytes.description: Declared size, checked against the runtime's 25 MB cap

TaskFileRef.title: TaskFileRef
TaskFileRef.description:
A reference to an already-uploaded Files API row attached to a task.

Bytes go through `POST /v1/files` first; a task only ever carries the
reference. The name is the workspace-relative path the runtime materializes
to under the task's files dir, so it is validated here rather than left to
the runtime's path guard — a 422 at the boundary beats a file silently
skipped at boot.

TaskInclude.title: TaskInclude
TaskInclude.description:
Opt-in, non-default enrichments for a task read (`GET /v1/tasks/{id}?include=`).

The default task read is the cheapest path: a single-row Postgres lookup with
no enrichment. Each value here names an extra projection that costs more than
that bare read (an extra round-trip or join) and so is only computed when the
caller explicitly asks for it. Repeatable: `?include=agent&include=...`.

- ``agent`` — live sandbox status for an interactive, in-flight task, read
  from the Restate task workflow (one extra round-trip).

TaskKind.title: TaskKind
TaskKind.description:
Discriminates the task execution shapes.

``agent`` boots the TypeScript runtime-agent image and runs an interactive
LLM agent. ``eval`` is the same execution shape run as an evaluation trial
(a Harbor task, a regression suite): it exists as its own kind so admission
and concurrency can be governed separately from production conversations
without inspecting metadata. ``process`` boots a one-shot Python script in
the separate runtime-process image and reports its result through the
existing RESULT event / completion-promise path. See
docs/design/process-tasks.md.

TaskPrompt.title: TaskPrompt
TaskPrompt.description: Cursor-style prompt payload for a task run.

TaskRecipePatch.title: TaskRecipePatch
TaskRecipePatch.description:
Operator-owned Recipe patch applied to one development Task.

The client supplies only File and checkout provenance. The Tasks service
resolves the checksum and complete spawn contract from trusted server
state before it persists the Task.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: Branch, tag, or full 40-character commit sha to check out. Omit it for the repository's default branch — the clone takes the remote's HEAD, so nothing has to be stored or kept in sync. An abbreviated sha is not recognised as a pin: it is passed to git as a branch name, so the clone fails and the repository is dropped.

depth.title: Depth
depth.description: Shallow-clone depth. 0 clones the full history.

TaskRepoRequest.title: TaskRepoRequest
TaskRepoRequest.description: One `POST /v1/tasks` `repositories[]` entry: a repository plus the state to clone it at.

id.title: Id
id.description: Run identifier. Use 'current' until task runs are persisted separately.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: Most recent activity timestamp for this run

TaskRun.title: TaskRun
TaskRun.description: Run-shaped view over the currently active task execution.

delivery_id.title: Delivery Id
delivery_id.description: Stable identity of this message across HTTP retries

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Optional caller intent. 'prompt' requests a fresh turn; 'steer' injects into the active turn and falls back to prompt if no turn is active.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Metadata patch merged into the task before dispatching the run.

runtime_id.title: Runtime Id
runtime_id.description: Runtime to rebind the task to if this run has to provision a new sandbox — resuming an idle task whose sandbox was reaped, or reopening a terminal one. Ignored while a sandbox is live, so a steer never changes version mid-turn. Omit to keep the task's existing pin.

files.title: Files
files.description: Files API references to attach to this turn. Materialized into the live sandbox before the turn runs (no restart needed) and merged into the task's conversation_files so a later restart replays them.

resume.title: Resume
resume.description: AG-UI resume entries answering the task's pending interrupt.

TaskRunCreate.title: TaskRunCreate
TaskRunCreate.description: Schema for creating a new run on an interactive task.

TaskRunResponse.title: TaskRunResponse
TaskRunResponse.description: Response returned after creating a task run.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Replaces the tag list wholesale (unlike metadata, which is merged). Omit to leave tags untouched; pass [] to clear them.

TaskUpdate.title: TaskUpdate
TaskUpdate.description: Schema for updating mutable task fields.

id.title: Id
id.description: Event ID (LogAttributes.event.id; the entity id for fold families)

TrackEvent.title: TrackEvent
TrackEvent.description: One arbitrary SDK track event projected through a stable family.

TrackPayload.title: TrackPayload
TrackPayload.description: One arbitrary event emitted through the SDK ``track()`` surface.

UploadCommand.title: UploadCommand
UploadCommand.description: Copy a Files API object of the project to ``path`` inside the sandbox.
